findings.risk: Prerendering /shop can trigger Stripe.js and analytics early. Gate side effects with document.prerendering and the 'prerenderingchange' event. Prerendered WebGL pages cost memory on low-end phones, so use 'moderate' rather than 'eager' for WebGL-heavy destinations.

findings.title: Price discovery inside the waitlist, and Teenage Engineering-style premium positioning (emerging bet)
findings.detail:
EMERGING. Teenage Engineering sustains prices of $1,999 or more (OP-1 Field) through playful industrial design, heavy constraints and artist adoption. In 2025 it ran 'pick your own price' experiments (OP-XY from €1,699 floors; OP-1 Field) to measure willingness to pay openly. Detent can do lighter price discovery without discounting:
(1) An optional third step in the waitlist form, shown to a random 20% of signups: a Van Westendorp 4-question block (too cheap, cheap, expensive, too expensive). This gives an acceptable price range per segment (editors vs producers vs developers) before deposit pricing locks.
(2) Test Founders pricing (+$50 vs +$80) across deposit waves, not within a wave, so no one sees two prices at once and fairness holds.
(3) Seed creator adoption: 30-50 named creators across the 5 audiences, each with a published haptic profile in the library. This is TE's artist-endorsement loop, adapted to software-defined haptics. Each creator page is shareable ('Feel how @editor scrubs a timeline').
findings.applyTo: The <capture-sheet> optional step (sampled). launch.ts {foundersPremiumByWave:[50,80]}. The /profiles/@creator pages in the feel-profile library, each with a 'Try it on the web dial' button and a 'Reserve with this profile preloaded' CTA.
findings.risk: Asking about price can anchor respondents, so sample only a subset and never show the form to people already in the deposit flow. Different prices across waves must be disclosed as 'wave pricing' to avoid fairness backlash. Creator seeding needs disclosure under the FTC rule.

antiPatterns: Fake countdown timers, invented 'X people viewing' widgets or fake reservation counters: they are named targets of the EU Digital Fairness Act (proposal due late 2026), deceptive under the FTC Act, and they destroy trust with skeptical creator audiences. Every counter needs a real data source and an 'as of' timestamp.

Fabricated or AI-written reviews and testimonials, or undisclosed beta-tester or employee reviews: FTC Consumer Review Rule, $53,088 per violation, enforcement began Dec 2025. On a concept site, label sample data as illustrative or leave it out.

A dummy third 'decoy' tier: replications show the decoy effect largely vanishes with realistic product pages (about 12% replication rate). Use two real editions, an honest default and a data-backed 'Most reserved' label.
Discount-led email capture ('10% off') on a premium product: it trains buyers to wait and undercuts the $349 anchor. Offer access, identity (serial choice) and exclusive haptic profiles instead.

Full-screen popups on load or on mobile exit-intent: they are demoted by Google on mobile, and exit-intent can't fire without a cursor. Trigger capture on engagement (turning the dial) as a small bottom sheet.
Rendering key facts only inside WebGL/canvas: crawlers, AI shopping agents and screen readers can't see them. Every spec and claim needs semantic HTML parity.
WebGL as the LCP element, or blocking the first paint on a 10 MB GLB: use an AVIF poster, lazy-load three.js, compress with Draco/Meshopt/KTX2, and keep a reduced-motion fallback.
Forcing account creation before purchase or reservation (18-26% abandonment): use guest checkout, then offer a passkey after purchase.
Showing 'ships Q1' or 'ships in 5-7 business days' in place of a calendar date: users miscalculate, and FTC rules require a reasonable basis and delay notices for paid preorders.
Using a manual-capture auth hold as a months-long 'deposit': holds expire after 7 days (30 with extended auth). Capture the deposit and refund on cancel.

Building in-agent checkout as the main agentic strategy: ChatGPT Instant Checkout was retired in March 2026 after converting about 3x worse than merchant sites. Make the catalog machine-legible and keep checkout on your own site.
Treating llms.txt as SEO: there is no measurable effect on search or citations. Ship it only for SDK docs used by coding agents.
A cart drawer or cart page for a single hero SKU: it adds a step with no comparison value. Put express wallets on the product page and treat accessories as checkout order bumps.
Letting the waitlist go stale for 3+ months before opening deposits: conversion falls from about 20% to under 10%.
Silently editing published promises (upgrade policy, subscription-free, price lock), as Whoop did in 2025: version the policies publicly with a changelog.
Polished CGI-only demos that outrun the real product (Rabbit r1, Humane): show unedited real-hardware video, a limitations section, and put reviewer units out before charging balances.
Subscription or cloud lock-in for core features on a premium hardware product (Humane's $24/mo): 'pay once, local-first, open SDK' is the differentiator.

Hard-coding launch dates, prices and batch sizes across pages: drive every phase, counter, JSON-LD block, feed and .ics file from the single launch.ts config so a slip updates everything consistently.

lens: What wins Awwwards, FWA, CSSDA and Webby awards for product and brand launch sites in 2024–2026, and how to apply it to Detent One. Sources are recent winners and nominees: Awwwards SOTY 2025 Lando Norris (OFF+BRAND) and Messenger (abeto), SOTY 2024 Igloo Inc (abeto), E-commerce SOTY 2024 Opal Tadpole, SOTD iyO, SOTM Apr 2026 Oryzo AI (Lusion), SOTM Jan 2026 Bruno Simon folio-2025, SOTM Feb 2026 Shopify Renaissance Edition. I also looked at hardware launches (Playdate, Teenage Engineering, Daylight DC-1, Rabbit r1, Analogue 3D, Nothing) and checked platform support as of Sep 2026 on webstatus.dev, WebKit, MDN and Codrops. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so a few claims below are my own judgment and are marked as such.

findings.title: Design to the scoring formula, and win the developer sub-scores where recent winners lose points
findings.detail: PROVEN. How Awwwards scores: Design 40%, Usability 30%, Creativity 20%, Content 10%. At least 18 jurors vote, the 3 outlier scores are dropped, and 6.5+ earns an Honorable Mention. Every SOTD winner then goes to a developer jury that scores six areas: Semantics/SEO, Animations/Transitions, Accessibility, WPO (performance), Responsive Design and Markup/Meta-data. A score above 7 earns the Developer Award. Recent product and launch SOTD scores are around 7.5–8.2, not 9+: Opal Tadpole 7.52 (Dev 7.84), iyO 7.68, Oryzo AI 7.86, Messenger 7.92, Igloo 7.92, Lando Norris 8.18. The developer sub-scores show a clear pattern. Winners max out Animations (Igloo 9.6, Messenger 9.0, Opal 8.6) but lose points on Accessibility and Semantics. Igloo, the 2024 Site of the Year, scored only 6.6 on Accessibility, 6.6 on Semantics/SEO and 6.4 on Markup, because its UI is rendered in WebGL. Messenger shows a WebGL site can still be fast (WPO 8.8, Responsive 8.4). Judges say they penalize: hero animation below 60fps, slow first load, missing focus states, ignoring reduced-motion, desktop-only thinking, placeholder copy, and inner pages that are weaker than the home page. CSSDA Website of the Day needs an average above 8.0. FWA (500+ jurors) rewards more experimental work.
findings.applyTo: Add a repo-level JURY.md checklist that mirrors the six developer sub-scores, and gate CI on it: Lighthouse mobile Performance ≥90, Accessibility 100, SEO 100, Best Practices 100; axe-core with zero violations; a Playwright smoke test on every route. Before submitting, test on a mid-tier Android phone (e.g. Pixel 6a or Galaxy A5x class) and confirm the hero holds 60fps. Build /profiles, /integrations and /for/* to home-page quality, since judges browse inner pages. Submit to CSSDA first, then Awwwards, then FWA.
findings.risk: Some reviewer blogs (e.g. hontran.dev) claim SOTD needs scores in the 'mid-to-high 8s', but the published winner scores above contradict that. Spend polish time on the 70% that Design and Usability cover rather than chasing Creativity alone.

findings.title: One interaction idea that is the product: the whole site is controlled by the dial
findings.detail: PROVEN. Recent Sites of the Year each have one physical idea you play with. Messenger: deliver mail on a tiny planet. Bruno Simon: drive a toy car, with achievements that unlock skins. Igloo: an iceberg metaphor, where one ice shard hides many ventures revealed as you descend. MDX puts it plainly: 'Strong single interaction concept beats multiple half-baked 3D elements', and juries read 'effects without a concept' as a lack of control. Playdate is the closest precedent for a hardware purchase: its store says 'Crank to buy', and the button fills fast at first and then slower as tension builds. Pressing A twice does the same thing for people who can't use the crank.
findings.applyTo: Build one global <detent-dial> web component that dispatches CustomEvent('detent', {detail:{index, profile, velocity, atEndStop}}). Each section listens for that event and maps rotation to its own parameter: the hero scrubs the exploded view, /profiles swaps the feel profile, /configure cycles finishes, and the headline weight follows rotation. The reserve step becomes 'Turn to reserve': three detents, then a virtual end-stop that thuds (sound plus a visual 4px overshoot), and then the CTA arms. A plain 'Reserve — $399' button must stay visible and clickable the whole time. Never put payment behind the ritual. Keep a normal top nav as well, because Usability is 30% of the score.
findings.risk: A gimmick that blocks the task will hurt Usability scores and conversion. Every dial-only action needs a click or keyboard equivalent, which WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 also requires.

findings.title: Render the hero in HTML first; the WebGL canvas is an enhancement layered on top
findings.detail: PROVEN. On a three.js hero the LCP element is usually the canvas, so a canvas that stays blank for 3 seconds gives an LCP of 3 seconds. Put the H1, the value line and the CTA in the DOM, and use as the LCP image an AVIF poster rendered from the same camera as the 3D first frame. Load the 3D bundle after the `load` event, reserve its box with CSS aspect-ratio, and keep crawlable text and the call to action in the DOM. The 2025 Web Almanac found 16% of pages still lazy-load their LCP image, which is the classic mistake. Targets used for award winners: LCP under 1.5s, CLS under 0.05, INP under 100ms, 60fps sustained, total weight under 3MB. Google's 'good' INP threshold is 200ms at p75.
findings.applyTo: In the hero markup: sits under . Start the renderer from addEventListener('load', () => (window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(boot)). Call await renderer.compileAsync(scene, camera), render one frame, then crossfade the canvas in over 400ms. Decode assets off the main thread (KTX2Loader's worker pool, MeshoptDecoder.useWorkers(2)). Add a
findings.risk: The poster must line up with the first 3D frame pixel for pixel (same camera and FOV), or the crossfade visibly jumps. Moving the whole renderer into an OffscreenCanvas worker is possible, but it complicates pointer handling for the dial. Keep rendering on the main thread and move only decoding to workers.

findings.title: No full-screen preloader: show content immediately and let the dial ring show 3D loading progress
findings.detail: PROVEN (the move away from gating preloaders). When a real page can paint in 200–300ms, a full-screen preloader only delays LCP and interaction, and some analyses now call it 'antiquated'. Every extra second of delay costs about 7% of conversions, and 53% of mobile users leave after 3 seconds. MDX's opposing point also holds: a blank canvas with no progress is unacceptable. The fix is to show progress only on the part that is still loading, never over the whole page. For returning visitors, cache the assets and skip any intro choreography.
findings.applyTo: While the glb and KTX2 files stream in, the poster's knob ring doubles as the progress bar: 24 tick marks light one by one, one per ~4% of bytes loaded, with an optional click per tick once sound is on. The page stays scrollable and the CTAs work the whole time. On GitHub Pages you cannot set Cache-Control headers (it serves a short max-age), so add a small Service Worker that caches /3d/*.glb, *.ktx2 and fonts cache-first, keyed by content hash. Set sessionStorage 'seenIntro' so the 1.2s intro camera move plays only once per session.
findings.risk: Check whether GitHub Pages compresses .glb and .ktx2 files (look at content-encoding in `curl -I`). Meshopt reaches its best ratios when gzip or Brotli is applied on top. If Pages serves them uncompressed, compare file sizes against Draco or gltfpack high-compression output. Service Workers also need careful versioning so users are not stuck with stale assets.

findings.title: 3D pipeline: three.js WebGPURenderer with TSL shaders, strict asset budgets, and a real aluminum material study
findings.detail: PROVEN plus a bet for the next decade. As of September 2025 WebGPU ships by default in Chrome, Edge, Firefox (Windows 141+, Apple Silicon macOS) and Safari 26 on macOS and iOS. `import { WebGPURenderer } from 'three/webgpu'` falls back to WebGL2 automatically. TSL (Three Shading Language) shaders compile to WGSL on WebGPU and GLSL on WebGL2; Bruno Simon's folio-2025 (SOTM Jan 2026) uses exactly this. Budgets from 2026 practice: under 100k vertices and about 100 draw calls on mobile; textures 1024px on mobile and 2048px on desktop. Use KTX2/Basis (ETC1S for base colour, UASTC for normals), which takes 4–8× less GPU memory than PNG, and meshopt geometry, which decodes faster than Draco. Keep the hero glb under 2MB compressed. Cap pixel ratio at 2 on desktop and 1.5 on mobile, and render post-processing at half resolution. Pre-compile with compileAsync, and pause rendering on visibilitychange and when the canvas leaves the viewport (IntersectionObserver). Postprocessing is what makes a scene 'look like film' rather than a demo (Lusion's EQS work). Apple's lesson: render exactly what communicates product value and nothing more.
findings.applyTo: The knob material is MeshPhysicalMaterial with anisotropy 0.7 and an anisotropyMap of radial and spiral lathe marks, so the highlight sweeps as the knob turns. Add a knurl normal map on the grip. The glass face uses clearcoat 1.0 with a thin dielectric layer. The round display is a 240×240 CanvasTexture showing the live profile UI. Light it with a small studio HDR converted through PMREM. The key light's azimuth follows the dial angle, so turning the dial visibly moves reflections. Add adaptive quality tiers: measure p90 frame time over the first 90 frames and drop a tier (DPR, then bloom, then shadows) if it exceeds 20ms. Commit a 3d-budget.json (max glb KB, texture count, draw calls) and fail CI if it is exceeded.
findings.risk: Firefox on Linux and Android does not have WebGPU yet, so the WebGL2 fallback path must be tested. WebGPU is not automatically faster for small scenes. Pin the three.js version: r186 removed some TSL exports and changed PBR energy conservation, so your visual look can change on upgrade. Upgrade deliberately and diff screenshots.

findings.title: The exploded view should carry the story as you scroll, not sit in the hero as a spinning object
findings.detail: PROVEN and moving. A single floating 3D object in the hero reads as dated in 2026. The shift is toward 3D as the storytelling layer, tied to scroll position. iyO's SOTD highlights were 'Interactive WebGL Exploded Views' and a colour-switch product slider. Shader.se (Codrops, May 2026) skips the entire render pass for any scene not in view and uses 'render offsets' to warm up the next scene before it appears. Apple still uses canvas image sequences (the AirPods Pro page scrubs 132 JPG frames) where real-time 3D would be overkill, which makes a good mobile fallback.
findings.applyTo: Use one persistent fixed canvas (position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none) behind normal DOM sections. Each section declares data-scene and a progress range. A single rAF loop reads progress from IntersectionObserver plus one getBoundingClientRect per frame, and damps only the camera (lerp 0.08–0.12), never the scroll itself. Exploded order, top to bottom: cover glass, then the 1.28-inch round display, the CNC knob shell, the BLDC gimbal motor, the 14-bit magnetic encoder (16,384 positions per turn), the PCB, and the weighted base. Each layer pairs with a short DOM caption placed via 3D-to-screen projection and transform:translate3d. The spec <dl> stays the crawlable source of truth. Cap each pinned sequence at about 250vh. Low-tier fallback: about 60 AVIF frames at 750px, loading every eighth frame first and filling in the rest later.
findings.risk: Very long pinned sections frustrate users and read as scroll-jacking. Labels positioned from 3D projection must not overlap on narrow screens, so switch to a stacked list under 480px.

findings.title: Keep native scrolling; use CSS scroll-driven animations as progressive enhancement
findings.detail: PROVEN (native scroll) plus a bet (CSS timelines). Old-style smooth scroll that translates a fixed container breaks the scrollbar, arrow keys, find-in-page and assistive tech. Lenis fixed that by easing the real scroll position, but it still conflicts with scroll-snap and changes how the OS scroll feels. CSS scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: scroll() and view(), plus animation-range) run on the compositor. Support: Chrome and Edge 115+, Safari and iOS 26+ (September 2025). webstatus.dev does not list Firefox as shipped, so the feature is still 'Limited' baseline. Within ten years it will cover all browsers, and scroll libraries will look like jQuery does today.
findings.applyTo: Skip the smooth-scroll library entirely. Write reveals as: @supports (animation-timeline: view()) { .reveal { animation: rise linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 10% cover 35%; } } @keyframes rise { from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(24px) } }. Outside @supports, content is simply visible in its final state. Animate only transform, opacity and clip-path. Drive WebGL progress from JS (the previous finding), not from CSS timelines, so every browser behaves the same.
findings.risk: Never hide content by default and rely on the animation to reveal it: in Firefox it would stay hidden. Test with @supports disabled.

findings.title: Page transitions: native cross-document View Transitions plus Speculation Rules, with no SPA router
findings.detail: A bet that is already production-safe as progressive enhancement. `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` gives animated multi-page navigation with no JavaScript router. Support: Chrome and Edge 126+, Safari and iOS 18.2+; Firefox not shipped; the feature is in Interop 2026. Gotchas: transitions only fire on same-origin, user-initiated navigations; they are silently aborted if the new page is not renderable within 4 seconds; names must be unique per document; snapshots default to object-fit: fill. Speculation Rules prerendering works in Chromium only; Safari has it behind a flag in 26.2 and Firefox does not ship it. Astro's own docs say its ClientRouter will 'increasingly become unnecessary'. Keeping the WebGL canvas alive across pages with Astro's transition:persist loses the WebGL context on Safari 18 (Astro issue #15727).
findings.applyTo: Set view-transition-name: detent-dial on both the small nav dial and the hero dial, so the knob morphs between pages. Set view-transition-name: product-shot on the clicked card only, assigned in a pageswap handler. Style ::view-transition-old(product-shot), ::view-transition-new(product-shot) with object-fit: cover. Add <link rel=expect href=#main blocking=render> on each page. Use the pageswap and pagereveal events to add a 'forward' or 'back' type, and style with :active-view-transition-type(). Add <script type=speculationrules>{"prerender":[{"where":{"href_matches":"/detent/*"},"eagerness":"moderate"}]}</script>, using the GitHub Pages base path. Do not boot WebGL or audio while document.prerendering is true; wait for the prerenderingchange event. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, use a 150ms crossfade only.
findings.risk: On each navigation the canvas is re-created, so re-initialisation must be fast: glb from the Service Worker cache, compileAsync, and the poster crossfade from finding 3. Firefox gets instant page swaps, which is acceptable. Check that the GitHub Pages repo base path matches every href_matches pattern.

findings.title: Sound that sells the feel: synthesised detent clicks, off by default, one tap to turn on
findings.detail: PROVEN that sound raises Creativity scores, with established etiquette. Igloo synced sound effects to particle motion. Bruno Simon commissioned CC0 tracks and uses single UI clicks with slightly varied playback rate. iyO lists sound as part of its SOTD build. Utsubo notes original audio 'significantly boosts creativity scores' when it adds meaning. Browsers in 2026 still require a user gesture to start an AudioContext, and autoplaying sound is a known UX failure. Feedback sound has to be close to zero latency or the illusion of touch breaks. For Detent, sound is the product demo itself: each profile has its own acoustic signature.
findings.applyTo: Create `new AudioContext({latencyHint:'interactive'})` lazily and call resume() inside the first pointerdown on the dial. Synthesise rather than ship sample files. Ratchet: a 20ms white-noise buffer through a bandpass filter (about 3.5kHz, Q about 8), with a gain envelope of 1ms attack and 30ms exponential decay. 12-click clock: a woody 1.8kHz variant. Fluid: low-passed noise whose gain follows angular velocity. Spring-return: a sine whose pitch rises with deflection. End-stop: a 140Hz sine thud with 80ms decay. Randomise filter frequency and playback rate by ±3%, scale gain with velocity, and allow at most one click per 12ms. Put a sound toggle in the header (aria-pressed, a 4-bar mini meter) and save the choice in localStorage. After the first dial turn, show a small inline chip 'Hear the detents?' instead of a modal. On Safari, set navigator.audioSession.type = 'ambient' where supported, so the site respects the silent switch and mixes with the user's music.
findings.risk: No background music by default. Any 'enter with sound' gate hurts conversion. Schedule clicks using audioCtx.currentTime and keep audio work out of the render loop.

findings.title: Web haptics in 2026: per-detent vibration on Android only, and one tick per real tap on iPhone
findings.detail: PROVEN constraints; this is a trap to design around. Android Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support navigator.vibrate (patterns in ms). It needs sticky user activation and does nothing in silent or Do Not Disturb mode. iOS Safari has never supported the Vibration API. The workaround was toggling a hidden <input type=checkbox switch> (Safari 17.4+). Apple's iOS 26.5 patch closed every programmatic re-tick path, so libraries now fire only the first tick of a pattern. What still works is a real, trusted tap on an invisible switch placed over the target, which gives a single tick. Scroll-triggered or drag-triggered haptics are dead on current iOS.
findings.applyTo: Android: while the dial is being dragged, call navigator.vibrate(10) per detent, throttled to at least 35ms apart; use [0,25,40,25] at end-stops. iOS: wire single-tap controls (the +/− step buttons, profile chips, 'Reserve') with a transparent <label> over a hidden <input type=checkbox switch>, so every tap produces a tick. Do not promise 'feel it on your phone'. Turn the limitation into copy instead: 'Your phone can only fake a detent. Detent One doesn't.' Wrap all of this in a single haptics.ts module and feature-detect.
findings.risk: Apple may close the remaining switch path in a later iOS release, so haptics must stay a pure enhancement with no function behind it. Overlays must not block scrolling (see ios-haptics PRs #12 and #13).

findings.title: Make the dial accessible: native range input underneath, WCAG 2.2 AA, and reduced-motion as a designed mode
findings.detail: PROVEN, and the easiest points to gain over past winners (Igloo scored 6.6 on Accessibility). WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements, AA) requires a single-pointer alternative for any drag interaction. A native <input type=range> is exempt because the browser provides the alternatives. Judges explicitly penalize missing focus states, missing reduced-motion handling and poor keyboard support.
findings.applyTo: Put a real <input type=range min=0 max=23 step=1 aria-label='Detent dial' aria-valuetext='Ratchet — detent 8 of 24'> under the 3D knob. Circular pointer drags on the canvas update input.value and dispatch an input event. Keyboard (arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End) and screen readers come for free. Add visible −/+ step buttons (at least 24×24 CSS px, per SC 2.5.8). The mouse wheel turns the dial only while it is focused or hovered with a fine pointer. At a virtual end-stop the dial releases the wheel so the page scrolls on, which mimics the physical stop. Use :focus-visible rings at 3:1 contrast, and make sure the sticky reserve bar never hides the focused element (SC 2.4.11). Under prefers-reduced-motion, camera flights become cuts, parallax is removed and view transitions become fades. Respect prefers-contrast and prefers-reduced-transparency. Any split-text animation keeps the real string in aria-label on the parent and marks the split spans aria-hidden.
findings.risk: A custom div with role=slider is doable but easy to get wrong. The native input is sturdier across screen readers and future-proof.

findings.title: Typography: one variable family, a mono for readouts, and headline weight tied to the dial
findings.detail: PROVEN restraint plus a bet on a signature move. Lusion's Oryzo uses one typeface family for about 99% of the site, so type supports the 3D instead of competing with it. Teenage Engineering is monospace only, with a 9/11/13/16/22/48px scale, all-caps labels at 0.12em tracking, tabular-nums for specs and zero radius. Nothing uses its dot-matrix Ndot face only for model names. One variable font file is roughly 100–200KB versus 400–800KB for equivalent static files. Headlines that change weight as you scroll are a 2026 trend, but kinetic type 'fights screen readers, fights search crawlers, and adds layout shift'. Animating font-variation-settings forces text re-layout; it is not a compositor-only change.
findings.applyTo: Use one variable grotesk with wght, wdth and opsz axes, plus one variable mono for numbers (angle, detent index, '16,384 positions/turn'). Register the axis: @property --wght { syntax:'<number>'; inherits:true; initial-value:400 }. Apply it only to a single hero word ('Feel') at font-variation-settings:'wght' var(--wght), set from dial rotation between 200 and 900, inside a fixed-width inline-block so nothing reflows. Alternatively, use a font with a GRAD (grade) axis, which changes stroke weight without changing width (e.g. Roboto Flex; my knowledge, not verified this session). Use text-wrap: balance on headings and pretty on body text. Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on specs and prices. Subset to Latin WOFF2, preload only the primary file, and use font-display: swap with a size-adjust fallback face so the swap causes no layout shift.
findings.risk: Limit axis animation to one element of 60 glyphs or fewer, or it will cost INP and frame time. Test for layout shift in Lighthouse and WebPageTest.

findings.title: A strict 2-colour palette with one accent that changes per feel profile
findings.detail: PROVEN. Recent winners use two dominant colours. Lando Norris: #D2FF00 and #111112. Opal Tadpole: #FFDB01 and #FFFFFF. Oryzo: #100904 and #FF8539. Shopify Renaissance: #F7F7EE and #292919. Igloo: #b6bac5 and #383e4e. Teenage Engineering caps itself at 5 colours, with #ff6600 reserved for action. Oryzo's rule, 'design cannot constantly ask for attention', lets the rendered product carry the colour. Art direction per section comes from lighting and material, not new colour systems.
findings.applyTo: Define tokens in OKLCH on :root: --ink (anodised near-black), --paper (warm off-white), --signal (a single hot accent reserved for Reserve and live state). Add a per-profile --profile-hue that the dial sets (e.g. Ratchet amber, Fluid cyan, Spring green, Clock white), used only on the round display, the knob's LED ring and a 1px progress rule. Derive tints with color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal) 20%, var(--paper)). Art-direct sections with the 3D lighting: a cold studio for engineering, warm desk light for the creator workflows, and a dark macro setup for the material study.
findings.risk: Profile colours must pass 4.5:1 contrast on text, or be used for decoration only. contrast-color() is only in Safari 26 so far, so don't depend on it.

findings.title: Mobile: redesign the dial for the thumb, not a shrunk desktop layout
findings.detail: PROVEN. Judges test on phones, and desktop-first layouts with breakpoints added later lose points; one source claims desktop-only thinking caps the score. Messenger 'works perfectly on mobile' (Responsive 8.4, WPO 8.8). Bruno Simon's folio switches to a lower-quality preset on mobile: no water blur, no depth of field, lower shadow resolution. One documented approach replaces the 3D hero with a WebP frame on mobile for instant LCP 'and identical brand recall'. Tilt input on iOS needs DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission(), called from a tap, over HTTPS.
findings.applyTo: On screens narrower than 768px the dial docks as a thumb-reachable disc at the bottom-centre of the hero, within the one-handed reach zone. A circular drag or a vertical swipe on the disc turns it, and step buttons sit either side. Default tier: DPR 1.5, no postprocessing, 1024px KTX2 textures. If the device is weak, detected via navigator.hardwareConcurrency ≤4 or measured frame time, use the AVIF image-sequence exploded view instead. Tilt-to-inspect the product is opt-in behind a 'Tilt to inspect' button that calls requestPermission. Use touch-action: none only on the disc so the page still scrolls everywhere else. Keep the sticky 'Reserve' bar inside safe areas using env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
findings.risk: Mobile Safari can lose the WebGL context under memory pressure, so handle webglcontextlost by falling back to the poster. Don't intercept scrolling on the disc's edges.

findings.title: Story order for a premium hardware page: show, don't tell, then engineering proof, then the price in context
findings.detail: PROVEN. Opal Tadpole won E-commerce Site of the Year 2024 as a mostly photographic single-page site with video-driven micro-demos ('The hand flip' hero, 'Explain it like I'm a 5 yo', 'Show don't tell' stats). Award-winning launch sites do not require heavy WebGL everywhere. Daylight DC-1 ('The computer, de-invented') used lifestyle photography, named-founder testimonials and 'In stock · Ships in 3–5 business days', and sold out $2.5M in days. Playdate states the $229 price late, after the reader understands what's included. Teenage Engineering sells with an engineering tone and a grid of specs. Oryzo puts the product on a lived-in creative desk rather than in a void. This matches a documented 2026 shift away from the standard hero/benefits/specs/reviews template.
findings.applyTo: Home page order: (1) Hook: the dial on a rendered real desk (keyboard edge, pen tablet, audio interface) with 'Feel the difference', which is immediately turnable. (2) Five-profile feel demo: you try it, the page changes with it, and each profile has one line of use-case copy. (3) Exploded engineering: CNC 6061 aluminum, BLDC gimbal motor, 14-bit encoder, the round display. This justifies the $349. (4) Workflows: 3 short loops each for editors, producers and 3D artists, linking to /for/*. (5) Open SDK and local-first, with a code snippet and a GitHub link, for trust. (6) Price with what's included and the Founders delta (+$50: serial-numbered and first batch). (7) FAQ with 6–8 questions. (8) Reserve. Keep the reserve CTA in a slim sticky bar after section 2.
findings.risk: Everything is fictional, so label concept content honestly. Fabricated testimonials, press quotes or scarcity counters would be deceptive and would read as template slop to jurors. Use clearly framed 'concept' or illustrative content instead.

findings.title: Build a campaign world beyond the site: the GitHub repo, a founder letter and the launch pages share one art direction
findings.detail: PROVEN in 2026 and good for virality. Lusion's Oryzo (Awwwards SOTM April 2026) treated an ordinary cork coaster as a serious AI product launch and carried the same craft to a GitHub page, a Product Hunt launch, a founder video and social content. Opal's homepage in 2026 is a manifesto-style essay ('the table'), not a product grid. Hardware demand at launch is real: Rabbit r1 sold 10k preorders on day one and about 50k in 5 days (a launch widely credited to its design), and Analogue 3D sold out in 8 minutes (black) and 10 minutes (white).
findings.applyTo: Tease page (phase 1): a playable one-screen dial with the manifesto letter underneath, 'Every input device you own is flat. Let's give software a feel.' The GitHub SDK repo README uses the same palette, type and a looping GIF of the dial, since the SmartKnob open-source community is the viral seed. Add a Product Hunt launch-day hero variant from the phase config (`phase: 'launch'` swaps the hero CTA, countdown and copy). Pre-generate share images per feel profile (/og/ratchet.png etc.).
findings.risk: Keep copy and assets consistent everywhere, because inconsistency across touchpoints reads as a template. Do not imitate real brands' trade dress.

findings.title: Reward play without a server: achievements, collectible profiles and share links in the URL
findings.detail: EMERGING, and shown to work in award winners. Bruno's folio-2025 has achievements that unlock vehicle skins and a timer for completing them all, plus a daily top-10 lap leaderboard and shared 'whispers'. Messenger adds light multiplayer presence with emoji. Playdate's digital gift-wrapping and its purple 'new game Monday' light turn content into rituals. On a static GitHub Pages site, shared live state needs a third-party backend; everything personal can stay local.
findings.applyTo: Add 'Feel Collection' achievements stored in localStorage: try all 12 profiles, hit an end-stop 10 times, find the hidden 'safe-cracker' profile (turn L-R-L to 3-7-2). Unlocks are cosmetic, such as a Founders colourway preview in /configure and an unlockable display face. Share links encode state in the URL hash (#p=ratchet&d=24&c=graphite), rendering a shareable card with a pre-built OG image per profile. Give each achievement a 1-second 'unwrap' on the round display, not a toast.
findings.risk: Live counters or presence (e.g. 'turns worldwide') need a realtime service, which breaks 'static only' and adds privacy obligations. Skip them or clearly label them. Keep achievements from blocking the purchase flow.

findings.title: Micro-interactions: every control behaves like a detent, with zero-latency feedback
findings.detail: PROVEN principle; specific values are my judgment. Winning launch sites highlight micro-interactions and transitions (Opal's microinteractions, Oryzo's intro, gallery and 3D-to-2D-to-3D transitions, iyO's colour-switch slider). Latency matters most: sound and visual feedback must land in the same frame as the input. JS cursor followers add lag and main-thread work; CSS cursors are free.
findings.applyTo: Buttons press 1px down (transform) with a detent click when sound is on, and :active must show within one frame. Transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). Keep all hover effects inside @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine). Change the cursor only over the dial, via CSS: cursor: url(/cursors/rotate.svg) 16 16, grab, and grabbing while dragging. Use no JS cursor follower and no magnetic buttons sitewide. Dial inertia uses a critically damped spring (e.g. stiffness 400, damping 40) that snaps to the nearest detent. The profile decides the spring, so Fluid glides and Ratchet snaps, and turning the dial teaches the product. Number readouts roll with tabular digits.
findings.risk: Over-animating every element makes the whole site feel slower. Keep 90% of the UI calm so the dial stays the star.

findings.title: A readability layer for machines: structured data, llms.txt and DOM text behind every canvas effect
findings.detail: EMERGING, and already paying off. A mid-2026 trend review found schema markup, llms.txt and agents.json became 'load-bearing', with 2,300 Bing Copilot citations for its author over three months. WebGL sites without server-rendered fallback text and FAQ schema are often invisible to AI search. Semantics/SEO and Markup are also two of the six developer sub-scores where SOTY winners lose points (Igloo 6.6 and 6.4).
findings.applyTo: Add JSON-LD: Product with two Offers (349 and 399 USD; availability PreOrder during the reservation phase, driven by the phase config), Organization, and FAQPage with 6–8 questions that also appear in the DOM. Add BreadcrumbList on /for/*, /profiles/* and /integrations/*. Give each route a unique title, meta description, canonical URL and OG image. Publish /llms.txt summarising the product, specs, price, SDK and links. Every WebGL label and spec has a DOM equivalent. Audit with Search Console URL Inspection → View Tested Page.
findings.risk: Schema must match what is visible on the page, or it can be ignored or penalised. Label the concept product clearly so the structured data does not misrepresent a real offer.

antiPatterns: Full-screen preloaders with a 0–100% counter before any content, and intro sequences that replay for returning visitors. They delay LCP and interaction; show progress only on the 3D stage.

Faking smooth scroll by translating a fixed container. It breaks the scrollbar, keyboard, find-in-page and assistive tech. Smooth-scroll libraries in general are becoming unnecessary; keep native scroll plus CSS scroll-driven animations.
One 3D product spinning in the hero with no purpose. By 2026 it reads as dated; 3D should carry the story as you scroll and respond to input.
Canvas-only UI and text, as in Igloo's WebGL UI, without DOM equivalents. It costs Semantics, Accessibility and Markup points (Igloo scored 6.6/6.6/6.4) and hides content from search and AI crawlers.
An empty canvas as the LCP element, or lazy-loading the LCP image (16% of pages still do).
Spline runtime embeds for the hero: 800KB–2MB of JavaScript runtime and Core Web Vitals failures on mobile.

Glassmorphism or backdrop-filter over animated WebGL: 15–30% FPS drops on real Android devices, plus the legibility backlash against Apple's Liquid Glass. Use opaque surfaces with a 1px hairline instead.
'Tech-bro' purple-to-blue gradient orbs and blobs behind the hero, and the default look of AI-generated images (including the overused yellow hue). Both read as template or slop to jurors.
Split-letter kinetic type on every heading: noise for screen readers, a problem for crawlers, and layout shift. Use at most one signature typographic move (the dial-driven weight).
Autoplaying sound, background music by default, or an 'Enter with sound' gate before content.
Relying on iOS web haptics for drag or scroll feedback. The iOS 26.5 patch broke programmatic re-ticks, so only single ticks from real taps work.

Keeping the WebGL canvas alive across pages with Astro ClientRouter transition:persist. Safari 18 loses the WebGL context (withastro/astro #15727). Prefer native cross-document View Transitions and fast re-initialisation.
Hiding content until a scroll animation reveals it. Firefox, which lacks animation-timeline, would show nothing; the default state must be visible.
Desktop-only experiences, or 'best viewed on desktop' notices. Judges test on phones and penalise this.

Magnetic buttons, JS cursor followers and infinite logo or text marquees used as filler. My judgment, not confirmed by search this session: they add main-thread cost and look like 2019–2023 agency templates.
Fabricated testimonials, press logos, 'only 3 left' counters or fake live-buyer popups on a concept product. They are deceptive, erode premium trust, and read as template slop to jurors.
Generic bento feature grids with no art direction. Bento is now the default layout, so it no longer differentiates without a strong concept inside the tiles.
Pinned scroll sequences taller than about 300vh that make users scroll endlessly to escape a section.

lens: Virality and gamification mechanics for product launches and brand websites, 2020-2026 plus emerging bets. Each finding is applied to Detent One on a static, client-side-only GitHub Pages site. Honesty rules: nothing is faked, anything that needs a server sits behind an adapter with a clearly labelled demo mode, and there are no invented counts, positions, reviews or scarcity.

findings.title: Feel Links: make the shareable artifact something the recipient can play with, not just an image (core viral loop, emerging bet)
findings.detail: Detent's most shareable thing is a feel. Encode a feel profile (detents per rev, detent strength, snap curve, end-stop angles, spring-return, sound pack, display face, finish) into a URL so the person who opens it gets the working 3D dial with synthesized clicks and Android haptics. They can then Remix it or Reserve one that feels like this. The proof points: Wordle went from 90 players (1 Nov 2021) to 300k+ (2 Jan 2022) to 2M+ weekly (9 Jan 2022) after the spoiler-free share was built in (Wardle added the share button around 16 Dec 2021), with 1.2M results shared on Twitter between 1 and 13 Jan 2022. neal.fun's playable toys draw about 9.6M visits a month. Why this should win over the next decade: a link that is itself a playable instance turns viewers into participants, and it costs nothing to serve. Figma, CodePen and Infinite Craft all show that playable links beat static screenshots. Implementation: path = nearest preset archetype, fragment = exact parameters, e.g. /f/ratchet-24/#v1.<base64url(compact JSON)>, kept under ~200 characters. The fragment never reaches a server, which is good for privacy. On decode, run the payload through a versioned schema (zod) and fall back to the archetype if it is invalid. Link unfurlers ignore the fragment, so the unfurl shows a build-time OG image for the archetype while the page itself shows the exact personal feel. Pre-render 12-16 archetype OG PNGs at build with Satori + resvg in an Astro endpoint (src/pages/og/[preset].png.ts using getStaticPaths). CTA copy: 'Feel this' (primary), 'Remix', 'Reserve one that feels like this'.
findings.applyTo: /f/[preset]/ route, the configurator's 'Share this feel' button, and profile cards in the library. Every Feel Link opens the hero <detent-dial> web component pre-loaded with the profile, plus a sticky Remix/Reserve bar.
findings.risk: Link previews on static hosting cannot be personalised, which is why the archetype-path trick is needed. Long fragments get truncated in some apps, so keep the payload compact (optionally CompressionStream('deflate-raw') and version prefixes). Treat decoded input as untrusted: clamp every numeric value so a malicious link can't produce ear-splitting audio or runaway vibration.

findings.title: Founder Pass: a personalised launch ticket rendered in the browser and shared as a file (proven pattern from Next.js Conf, Vercel Ship and Supabase)
findings.detail: Personalised tickets are a proven developer-launch loop. Vercel generated 100k+ Next.js Conf tickets at about 800ms each with dynamic OG images. Supabase Launch Week 5 produced 3,000+ tickets and added a Golden Ticket swag mechanic (secret ticket URLs such as ?secret=true). On a static site the equivalent has to be built client-side. Render the pass to <canvas>/OffscreenCanvas from an SVG template. It shows the handle the user types (never auto-pulled), their chosen finish, a generative 'feel signature' ring (a deterministic radial waveform built from a hash of their feel profile) and a pass ID. Export two sizes, 1200x630 (X/LinkedIn) and 1080x1920 (Stories), with convertToBlob(). Call await document.fonts.ready before drawing. Share with navigator.canShare({files:[file]}) followed by navigator.share({files,text,url}). Fallbacks: navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'image/png': blobPromise})]), plus an <a download> link and a 'Copy link' button. For the screen-recordable wow moment, tilt the on-page pass with the pointer and animate a holographic foil using a CSS @property --angle on a conic-gradient with mix-blend-mode: color-dodge, and disable it under prefers-reduced-motion. Burn the URL (detent.one/pass) into the image so reposts still attribute.
findings.applyTo: /pass. It is shown after waitlist signup, becomes the 'Reservation Pass' after a deposit, and is reused on /launch during launch week.
findings.risk: Web Share support is uneven: Safari has full support, Chrome on desktop is partial, and Firefox has none, so the download/clipboard fallback is required. Pass IDs must not pretend to be sequential or scarce. In demo mode show 'DEMO-7K3Q' style random IDs. In live mode, use the real reservation number issued by the payment backend. Only print a unit serial on the pass if Detent really will engrave it.

findings.title: Referral waitlist: use milestone rewards (Harry's) and real shipping batches, not a vanity queue number (Robinhood)
findings.detail: The numbers: Harry's collected 100k+ emails in one week (about 85k valid). 77% came from referrals (about 65k emails from about 20k referrers). Tiers were 5 referrals for shave cream, 10 for a razor, 25 for a premium set and 50 for a year free, and 200+ people hit 50. Robinhood got about 1M signups before launch by showing people their queue position and letting them jump it through referrals (widely reported; about 3 referrals per user according to secondary sources). Waitlister's dataset gives an 11% median waitlist conversion against a 6.6% all-industry landing-page median (Unbounce Q4 2024). Only about 7% of waitlists use referrals at all. A K-factor of 0.3-0.7 is healthy. Dual-sided rewards lift participation about 29% and tiered rewards about 27% (Rivo). 83% of people say they are willing to refer but only 29% do, so the reward has to be concrete. For a $349 hardware product: (a) Queue position should mean something real, namely which manufacturing batch you are in ('Batch 1 ships first'). Show it only if batches are genuinely allocated in signup/referral order. (b) Use milestone tiers sized to a smaller, high-intent audience: 1 referral unlocks an exclusive 'Founders' display face; 3 unlock a sound pack plus your name in the device's firmware credits screen (Arc-style early-adopter credits); 5 move you up one batch; 10 earn a machined brass knob cap. Most rewards are digital, cheap to deliver and valuable to the owner, so there is no discounting that erodes the premium. (c) Make it dual-sided: the friend gets the Founders face too. (d) Count a referral only after the invited person confirms their email (double opt-in), and apply IP/device heuristics at the top tiers, as Harry's did. Static implementation: a WaitlistAdapter interface with join(email, ref) and status(token), and two implementations. DemoAdapter writes to localStorage behind a persistent banner: 'Concept demo: nothing was sent; referral progress can't be tracked in the demo'. LiveAdapter posts to any provider or a Worker. The referral code is 8 characters of Crockford base32 from crypto.getRandomValues, never the email. On landing with ?r=CODE, store it in sessionStorage, show 'A friend saved you a spot + the Founders face', and carry it through to reservation. Share copy should be pre-written per audience (editors, producers, designers, developers, streamers).
findings.applyTo: /waitlist, the post-signup /pass dashboard (a milestone ladder drawn as detent ticks around a dial, filling in as each tier is reached), and the ?r= handler in the global layout. Phase is controlled by src/config/launch.ts (phase: tease|waitlist|reserve|launch|live; mode: demo|live).
findings.risk: A client-side-only site cannot count referrals, so the demo must never show invented numbers or positions. The FTC Act and the 2024 rule on fake social-influence indicators make fabricated counts a real liability. Referral rewards must never be tied to reviews. Queue-jumping without real product value is the Clubhouse trap, covered in the anti-patterns list.

findings.title: Refundable deposit reservation with one-click cancel and legally sound delivery promises
findings.detail: A deposit list predicts revenue; an email list only predicts reach. BoostYourCampaign's reservation-funnel guide says email subscribers convert to buyers in the low single digits while deposit holders convert 'several times higher', often most of the list. It recommends deposits of $5-$25 scaled to price, e.g. $25 on a $400 product (directional, no hard data). Framework's model is the one to copy: the deposit secures your place, is credited against the final price, the balance is charged at ship time, and cancelling refunds the full deposit. For Detent: a $25 refundable deposit (optionally $49 for Founders Edition, which reserves the engraving and the price lock). US law: the FTC Mail, Internet or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule (16 CFR 435) requires a reasonable basis for any stated ship date (or 30 days if none is stated). If a date slips, you must send a delay notice with a definite revised date and an option to cancel for a full refund, and refund card payments within 7 working days. Amazon's record $2.5B FTC settlement (25 Sep 2025) over the Prime 'Iliad' cancel flow shows what hard-to-exit flows cost. So cancellation is one click from the reservation email and from /reserve/manage, with no save-offer maze. Tariffs: US de minimis ended 29 Aug 2025, and Kickstarter added a Tariff Manager in April 2025. Show an all-in price that includes duties, or state the duties line up front. Static implementation: link out to hosted checkout (Stripe Payment Links or Shopify checkout). In demo mode the CTA opens a mock checkout sheet (a <dialog> with a 'Demo, no charge' watermark) and issues a DEMO pass. The UI shows the ship window per batch, the price lock, 'Refundable anytime before shipping, one click', and a deposit ledger.
findings.applyTo: /reserve and /reserve/manage (demo). Deposit holders get 24-hour early access on launch day.
findings.risk: Deposits are a regulated money flow, so the live mode needs real terms and privacy pages plus proper delay-notice email templates. Don't state ship dates you can't back up. A countdown to the reservation opening is fine only if the event is real and fixed.

findings.title: Screen-recordable 'toy mode' with a built-in clip recorder: design for X/TikTok reposts
findings.detail: Hardware and web toys spread through video. SmartKnob's March 2022 reveal 'made quite a splash' (Hackaday) on a ~10-second clip of virtual detents. Flipper Zero's TikTok clips (switching off store TVs) pushed a $4.8M, 37k-backer Kickstarter into mainstream awareness. Bruno Simon's Folio 2025 (three.js with TSL, so it runs on WebGPU where available with a WebGL fallback, Rapier physics, achievements, multiplayer whispers) was Awwwards Site of the Month in January 2026. Awwwards Sites of the Year: 2025 went to Messenger (abeto, a tiny WebGL planet you make deliveries on) and Lando Norris (OFF+BRAND); 2024 included Opal Tadpole, a hardware webcam product site that also won E-commerce Site of the Year 2024, which is the closest precedent to Detent. Implementation: a /toy route with a full-bleed dial, ?clean=1 to hide all chrome, and a 9:16 safe area so phone screen-recordings look native. Physics should have inertia plus magnetic snap to detents, and each detent should fire three signals together: a Web Audio click (a 3-8ms filtered noise burst with a pitch that varies per profile), a display-face tick and a camera micro-shake. Add a 'Record 6s' button: canvas.captureStream(60), plus an audio track from AudioContext.createMediaStreamDestination(), merged into new MediaStream([...v.getTracks(), ...a.getTracks()]). Pick the format by testing MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported('video/mp4;codecs=avc1.42E01E,mp4a.40.2') first and falling back to 'video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus'. Burn a 'detent.one/toy' watermark into the frames, then share via Web Share with files. Audio starts only after the first user gesture; show a visible 'Sound on' affordance.
findings.applyTo: The hero dial on / (the page reacts to rotation), a dedicated /toy route, and the Record button on the configurator and Feel Links.
findings.risk: Recording format support varies by browser: Safari records MP4 natively, and some Chromium builds support only WebM, so check at runtime and never promise MP4. Recording costs GPU time, so lower the pixel ratio while recording. Respect prefers-reduced-motion (swap to a static turntable). Provide a keyboard and screen-reader path: an ARIA slider role with arrow keys stepping one detent.

findings.title: Web haptics reality check: audio is the main 'haptic', and vibration is a progressive enhancement
findings.detail: navigator.vibrate works in Android Chrome only. iOS Safari has never implemented it, and desktop browsers do nothing. From Safari 17.4, iOS gave a haptic tick when an <input type=checkbox switch> was toggled, and libraries such as ios-haptics triggered it with programmatic label clicks. Apple closed that programmatic path in iOS 26.5. What still works is an invisible switch overlay under a real finger tap (isTrusted), and on 26.5+ multi-tick patterns fire only their first tick. Rules for Detent: (1) The Web Audio click is the primary feedback channel, and it should be good enough to carry the experience with sound alone. (2) On Android, call navigator.vibrate(8-12) per detent, throttled to at most one call per 30ms, with a user toggle. (3) On iOS, put switch overlays only on discrete tap targets (the dial's press-to-select button, the Daily Detent answer buttons). Never promise continuous haptics during rotation. (4) Copy should frame it honestly: 'Your phone can only hint at it. Detent One has a motor that pushes back.' That gap becomes the reason to reserve rather than a disappointment.
findings.applyTo: A shared haptics module (src/lib/feedback.ts) used by <detent-dial>, /toy, /daily and the configurator. Capability detection: 'vibrate' in navigator, plus iOS UA/feature detection for the switch overlay.
findings.risk: The iOS switch technique relies on non-standard behaviour Apple has already restricted once. Isolate it behind a feature flag so it can be removed in one line. Excessive vibration drains battery and is an accessibility problem, so default to off under prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.title: Honest social proof: show only counters you don't control, and no testimonials for a product that doesn't exist yet
findings.detail: The FTC Trade Regulation Rule on Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (effective 21 Oct 2024, 5-0 vote) bans fake or AI-generated reviews and testimonials. It bans insider reviews without clear disclosure, company-controlled 'independent' review sites, review suppression, and buying or selling fake indicators of social-media influence. It also bans incentives conditioned on a particular sentiment ('tell us how much you loved it and get $5' is illegal; neutral review incentives may still need disclosure). Civil penalties were up to $51,744 per knowing violation at adoption, inflation-adjusted each year. Detent is a concept, so it has no customer testimonials. Use verifiable signals instead: (a) live GitHub stars and forks for the open SDK, fetched client-side from https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} (unauthenticated limit is 60 requests/hour per IP; cache in sessionStorage; hide the widget on failure rather than showing a stale or made-up number); (b) giscus reactions and comments from GitHub Discussions on library profiles; (c) open-source lineage credit ('Inspired by Scott Bezek's SmartKnob, Apache-2.0'), which earns trust with the HN audience; (d) press and creator quotes only after they exist, each with a same-place, same-format disclosure if a free unit was given. Put a persistent site-wide 'Concept product' disclosure in the footer and on /about.
findings.applyTo: Social-proof slots on /, /for/*, /library and /reserve. A <gh-stars> web component, the giscus embed, and the footer disclosure.
findings.risk: The GitHub API rate limit and outages mean the widget has to fail silently. Don't pad the numbers (no 'and counting', no floors). Displaying user reviews in marketing turns them into testimonials, which lose the protections that apply to hosted reviews.

findings.title: Ethical guardrails as a selling point: publish an /honest page and design out dark patterns
findings.detail: Regulation is catching up with manipulative design. The FTC's 2022 report 'Bringing Dark Patterns to Light' names fake countdown timers, false scarcity, disguised ads, hard-to-cancel flows, buried fees and tricks to collect data. Amazon paid $2.5B in September 2025, and by September 2026 more than $845M had been refunded. Poland's consumer regulator fined Amazon €7.48M over countdown timers. The EU Digital Fairness Act proposal (consultation July-October 2025; proposal expected Q4 2026) targets fake urgency, addictive design, influencer marketing and unfair personalisation. The hype-then-backlash cases point the same way. Clubhouse lost about 80% of its users within months of invite-driven hype. Rabbit r1 sold 10k preorders on day one (20 times its internal target) and then suffered backlash when the shipped product didn't match the demos. Rules for Detent: countdowns only to real fixed events, computed from a UTC timestamp in launch.ts. No stock or 'X people viewing' indicators. No confirmshaming (the decline button reads 'Not now', not 'No thanks, I like boring knobs'). No pre-checked add-ons. Deposit refunds in one click. All-in pricing. Every product video is labelled ('Real-time render', 'Prototype, production firmware'). Game mechanics never punish (streak freezes, no loss-framed notifications, no loot boxes). A full 3D-free path via reduced-motion and keyboard. List these commitments on /honest and link it next to every CTA as 'Our launch promises'. Premium buyers treat trust as part of the price.
findings.applyTo: The /honest page, the CTA microcopy system, launch.ts timestamps, and the reserve, checkout and cancel flows.
findings.risk: Being honest means giving up some short-term conversion levers (fake urgency does lift clicks), so A/B tests shouldn't be judged on first-session conversion alone. Track deposit refund rate and 90-day referral quality as well.

findings.title: Monzo-style Skip Passes: give invites to people who have committed, not to everyone
findings.detail: Monzo gave each user one single-use Golden Ticket after about two weeks of active use. Tom Blomfield says Golden Tickets produced about 40% of 2017 signups at zero cost. Monzo also found that users with 3+ friends on the app had 70% day-90 retention against 50% for users without. The insight: the best referrers are people who have already committed. For Detent, each deposit holder gets 2 Skip Passes. A Skip Pass takes a friend straight to reservation at the referrer's batch, and both sides get the Founders display face. Codes are single-use and expire 14 days after launch (a real, stated deadline). This is not artificial scarcity: the constraint is real batch capacity, and the copy says so ('Batch 1 is 2,000 units; each reserver can bring 2 friends into it'), but only if that is true. Monzo's messaging data is useful too: 'Help us build a bank you'd be proud to call your own' beat benefit messaging by 300%. For Detent, test 'Help us tune the first software-defined knob'. Static implementation: in live mode the payment or waitlist backend mints codes, and the site's /s/CODE route only reads and forwards them. In demo mode, show the UI with obviously fake 'DEMO-XXXX' codes.
findings.applyTo: The post-deposit /pass dashboard ('Your 2 Skip Passes'), the /s/[code] landing variant, and the reservation confirmation email copy.
findings.risk: Skip Passes only work if the waitlist is actually longer than a batch. If demand is thin, drop the mechanic rather than inventing a queue. Monzo's own failures (campus ambassadors, local business partnerships, hackathons that brought about 300 users) show not every channel is worth running.

findings.title: Launch Week with daily reveals and ticket stamps, where the build pipeline enforces the schedule
findings.detail: Supabase and Vercel turned launch weeks into events. There are five days of reveals, each personalised ticket accumulates status, and golden tickets are unlocked through secret URLs (Supabase LW5 produced 3,000+ tickets, with swag for winners). Detent schedule: Day 1 'The Feel Engine' (the motor plus a 14-bit encoder explainer with a live torque graph), Day 2 'The Face' (the round 1.28" display and watch-face gallery), Day 3 'Open SDK' (repo goes public, which is the HN day), Day 4 'Integrations' (Premiere, Resolve, Ableton, Figma, Blender, VS Code, OBS), Day 5 'Founders Edition and price'. Each day's visit adds a stamp to the Founder Pass (stored in localStorage; the stamp animation is a detent click). Five stamps unlock a holographic pass finish, a cosmetic reward with no purchase needed. The static-site integrity trick: a GitHub Actions scheduled workflow (on.schedule cron at the reveal hour in UTC) rebuilds and deploys, and launch.ts only includes content whose revealAt is at or before the build time. Unrevealed content is therefore not in the bundle, so there is nothing to spoil and no fake client-side lock that curious users could bypass through devtools.
findings.applyTo: /launch plus the per-day sections, launch.ts (revealAt per section), .github/workflows/deploy.yml (a schedule trigger added to the push trigger), and the stamps on /pass.
findings.risk: GitHub Actions cron can run minutes late under load, so schedule 10-15 minutes early and describe times as 'around 9am PT'. A prize drawing tied to stamps is a sweepstakes: it needs official rules, a free alternative method of entry, and, in NY and FL, registration and bonding when total prizes exceed $5,000. Cosmetic-only rewards avoid all of that.

findings.title: Daily Detent: a Wordle-style daily puzzle that teaches the product's value and shares as text
findings.detail: Wordle's share grid was the viral unit: spoiler-free, competitive and readable at a glance, and it works on every platform because it is plain text. Detent version: each day you hear (and on Android feel) a hidden feel profile, then identify it in 5 tries on a dial of choices (detent count, spring-return versus free, end-stop angle). The share text looks like 'Detent #37 ●●◐○○ 3/5 detent.one/daily'. Everyone gets the same puzzle via seed = floor((Date.now() - EPOCH_UTC) / 86400000). The puzzle list is generated at build time, and answers are stored as SHA-256 hashes checked with crypto.subtle.digest, so the list can't be trivially spoiled. Streaks live in localStorage with one free 'freeze' per week (a gentle mechanic, no loss-framing). Why it matters for conversion: a person who plays for a week learns the vocabulary of software-defined feel (ratchet, detent density, end-stops), which is exactly what justifies $349. The final screen offers 'Feel today's profile in the configurator'.
findings.applyTo: /daily, a link from the hero, and a #daily-detent channel in Discord. Share via navigator.clipboard.writeText plus Web Share (text).
findings.risk: Telling profiles apart by audio alone may be too hard. Tune difficulty with playtests and include visual torque-curve hints on tries 3-5. Any hashed-answer scheme can be brute-forced by determined users given a small answer space; that's fine here because it's a toy, and spoilers still spread the game.

findings.title: Exploration achievements ('Detents found: n/24') whose rewards are real device customisations
findings.detail: Bruno Simon's Folio 2025 and Awwwards' recent Sites of the Year (Messenger, Igloo Inc) reward curiosity with discoverable content and an achievements system. On a marketing site, visible progress raises depth of visit, and every extra interaction adds belief in the product. Detent design: a small progress ring in the corner, styled as the dial's own tick marks, fills as you find 24 'detents'. Examples: turn 1,000 detents in total; find the hidden 13th click on the 12-click clock profile; try all 5 /for/ audience modes; open the SDK docs; view the model in AR (<model-viewer> with iOS Quick Look USDZ); navigate the whole hero by keyboard (an accessibility achievement that rewards inclusive use); enter a safe-combination gesture (L3, R5, L2 detents). Rewards are cosmetic unlocks in the configurator, such as an exclusive 'Signal Orange' anodisation preview, secret display faces and sound packs. Items marked 'ships to your device' are delivered only if they are genuinely included, carried by the reservation code. Implementation: localStorage in try/catch, BroadcastChannel to sync tabs, and toasts via the Popover API (popover="manual") with an aria-live=polite mirror. An /achievements page lists every item with hints so nothing is gated behind pixel-hunting.
findings.applyTo: The global layout (<achievement-ring> web component), the configurator's unlockables, /achievements, and the end-of-session recap.
findings.risk: Too many toasts get annoying. Cap them at 1 per 20 seconds and let users mute. Never tie achievements to purchase or to discounts that change price perception. Storage can be cleared or blocked (private mode), so the site must work fully without it.

findings.title: Feel-profile library as a GitHub-native UGC growth loop (the Elgato Marketplace pattern, without a backend)
findings.detail: Control-surface ecosystems grow through what the community creates. Elgato's Marketplace holds thousands of plugins, profiles and assets from verified community makers, and SmartKnob spawned many open-source forks. Static implementation: store profiles as profiles/*.json in the public repo and accept contributions as pull requests. CI validates each file with JSON Schema (ajv) plus a numeric clamp check, renders its OG card with Satori at build, and deploys. Each /library/[slug] page shows the author's GitHub handle and avatar, a 'Try it' button that loads the 3D dial, a 'Remix' button that opens the configurator pre-filled (with forkedFrom lineage recorded in the JSON), a 'Copy SDK snippet' button, and giscus for discussion. Engagement signals are real because they come from GitHub (reactions and comments) rather than a made-up install count. Seed the library with 40 official profiles covering the five audiences (Premiere J/K/L scrub, Resolve jog, Ableton filter sweep with end-stops, Logic fader, Figma zoom, Blender frame scrub, VS Code scroll-by-function, OBS volume with a 0 dB detent). A weekly 'Feel Friday' feature gives winners a badge and a spot on the homepage, which is a reward of status rather than a discount. Why it works: each contributed profile is new SEO surface, a new Feel Link to share, and proof that the SDK is open.
findings.applyTo: /library, /library/[slug], profiles/ in the repo, and .github/workflows/validate-profiles.yml. The 'Submit a profile' CTA points to a pre-filled GitHub new-file URL.
findings.risk: PR moderation takes effort. Use CODEOWNERS and a template, and require a schema pass. Contribution requires a GitHub account, which puts off non-developers. Later, provide an 'Export JSON' plus a GitHub Discussions form for non-devs. Clamp all numeric values so malicious profiles can't create harmful audio or vibration.

findings.title: Coordinated launch-platform playbook: HN for the open SDK, Product Hunt for craft, D2C deposits (not Kickstarter) for money
findings.detail: Hacker News: post as 'Show HN: Detent – open-SDK haptic knob with software-defined detents'. Use factual language, no marketing voice, and link to the SDK repo or a technical write-up, not the shop. Early vote velocity matters most: 10 votes in the first 15 minutes beats 50 over 6 hours. Post Tuesday-Thursday 8-10am PT, and have the founder answer every comment. Vote rings are detected and get accounts banned. Product Hunt: third-party analyses report only about 10% of launches get featured in 2025 (down from 60-98% in 2020-23). Featuring is judged on Useful, Novel, High craft and Creative, which suits Detent's craft. Launch at 12:01am PT, write a maker's first comment with the story and a Feel Link, and treat substantive comment replies as the main signal. Build 200-400 real supporters from established accounts over 4-6 weeks, and never ask for upvotes directly. Kickstarter benchmarks for context: 20-31% of prelaunch followers become backers; about 29% of funds arrive on day 1; the first and last 72 hours bring 50-60% of pledges. Kickstarter added a Tariff Manager in April 2025. Recommendation: run D2C refundable deposits so Detent owns the customer list, with Kickstarter optional only for a Founders Edition batch. Sequence: T-14 days HN (SDK open-sourced); T-7 creator embargo briefing; T0 at 9am PT reservations open to deposit holders 24 hours early, then everyone; T+1 Product Hunt (keep it off T0 so the team can answer comments); T+2 Discord AMA.
findings.applyTo: /launch (timeline component driven by launch.ts), /press, the SDK README, and the PH maker comment.
findings.risk: The PH and HN numbers come from practitioner blogs, not official platform data, so treat them as directional. Hardware on PH usually needs an existing audience. HN reacts badly to vaporware, so a real public repo and a working web demo are the price of entry.

findings.title: Creator seeding with one embargo moment, a static press kit, and FTC-compliant disclosure
findings.detail: Hardware launches reach people through creators. Flipper Zero broke out after Adam Savage's review and a wave of organic TikToks, and Apple's model is an embargoed wave where every creator posts in the same hour. Plan: send 60-100 production-intent units to mid-tier creators (100k-1M subscribers; paid integrations run about $2k-$25k, or seed plus affiliate) spread evenly across editors, producers, designers/3D artists, developers and streamers. Brief them 4-6 weeks out, with a single embargo lift at T0 9am PT. A static /press kit carries 4K B-roll, the GLB/USDZ model, sound-pack WAVs, fact sheet, logo SVGs and the creator's own signed feel profile published in the library (e.g. /library/creator-slug). Each creator gets a unique ?r= code and a Feel Link, which gives honest attribution without any tracking pixels. FTC 2023 Endorsement Guides: a free unit is a material connection. Disclosure must be unavoidable and in the same place and format as the endorsement; '#ad' alone may not be enough, and a 'click for more' or profile-bio disclosure is not. The brand must monitor creators' posts even if it never asked for coverage, so the seeding agreement requires disclosure and allows negative reviews (anything else would amount to review suppression).
findings.applyTo: /press (static page plus zip downloads from GitHub Releases), a creator section in /library, and ?r= codes per creator.
findings.risk: Seeded units can leak before the embargo, so plan for a leak by making the teaser phase a deliberate 'leak' of the silhouette only. Budget for units that are never returned. Unflattering reviews will happen; the fix is to ship firmware that matches the demo (the Rabbit r1 lesson).

findings.title: Discord activation wired to the site's five audiences
findings.detail: A community carries a hardware brand between launch and shipping. Monzo put the community to work through a public roadmap, 12,000 community name suggestions and 'help us build' messaging. Discord's native Onboarding needs at least 7 default channels, at least 5 of them open to @everyone for viewing and posting. It supports 3-5 customisation questions that assign roles and channels, and Advanced mode lets you write the questions yourself. Setup: Q1 'What will you turn?' (Editing / Music / Design & 3D / Code / Streaming) maps to role and channels, mirroring the /for/ pages. Q2 'Reserved?' (Yes / Not yet) maps to a Founders role verified later. Q3 'Want to build?' (SDK tinkerer) maps to #sdk-dev. Core channels: #feel-lab (paste Feel Links, which unfurl with archetype OG images), #daily-detent, #show-your-setup, #sdk-dev, #firmware-roadmap (public), #launch-week. Discord invite links can't carry query parameters, so create one invite code per audience and per /for/ page to attribute joins honestly using Discord's own invite-use counts. The 'Join the Feel Lab' CTA should appear only after a value moment (after waitlist signup and on Feel Link pages), not in the main nav before the product has earned it.
findings.applyTo: The CTA on /pass after signup, the footer, /for/* pages (each with its own invite code), and /library.
findings.risk: An empty Discord is anti-social proof. Open it only once there are about 200 seeded members (creators, SDK testers, team), and staff it daily through launch. Moderation is also a cost.

findings.title: 'Your Detent Session': a Wrapped-style identity recap at the end of exploration, computed on-device
findings.detail: Spotify Wrapped 2025 reached 200M+ engaged users within 24 hours (up 19%; 2024 took 62 hours to get there) and 500M+ shares on day one (up 41%). Its format is a 9:16 story with a share button on every card and statistics recast as identity: people want to belong and to stand out (optimal distinctiveness). For Detent: after meaningful engagement (at least 200 detents turned, or 3 achievements), offer a 5-card recap covering detents turned, time to first click, favourite profile, achievements found and an archetype. Use 8-12 deterministic archetypes derived from behaviour, such as 'The Ratchet: precise, decisive', 'The Fluid: continuous thinker', 'The Clockmaker: loves structure'. Render client-side at 1080x1920 and 1200x630 and share via Web Share with files. Everything is computed locally from session data, with no uploads, which also demonstrates Detent's local-first value. Operational phase later: the companion app generates an annual 'Detent Year' on-device (opt-in) from local usage, e.g. 'you scrubbed 41 km of timeline'.
findings.applyTo: A <session-recap> component shown from the achievement ring or when exit-intent scrolls to the footer. Archetype OG images are pre-rendered at /recap/[archetype] for link unfurls.
findings.risk: Don't interrupt people with a modal. Offer the recap only through an explicit button or at the natural end of the page. Archetype copy should flatter without being manipulative, and never imply scarcity ('only 3% get this').

findings.title: Teaser-phase puzzle trail with rewards verified by cryptography, so nothing secret sits in the bundle
findings.detail: Puzzle hunts and ARGs are having a comeback as launch teasers: KFC's 11 Secrets puzzle hunt, the SCXR fashion ARG (2025), and the 'Return to Silent Hill' ARG (January 2026) spread clues across Reddit, Instagram and TikTok leading to a hub site. Supabase hid golden tickets behind secret URLs. For Detent's tease phase: the knob's round display shows glyphs in the teaser video, and clues are spread across the video, HTML comments in the source, /humans.txt, the SDK docs and a Discord pin. They resolve to a safe-dial combination entered on the hero dial. Verification: SHA-256 hash comparison of salt + answer via crypto.subtle.digest. The reward payload (a secret page slug and, in live mode, a store coupon) is encrypted with AES-GCM using a key derived from the answer via PBKDF2 (≥200k iterations), so the reward can't be pulled out of the JS bundle without solving the puzzle. Scarcity must be real and enforced server-side, for example a store coupon capped at 500 redemptions with the cap stated publicly ('first 500 solvers'). Prefer rewards that don't cheapen the price, such as a secret colourway in the Founders batch or a name in the firmware credits. Expect the solution on Reddit within hours. That spreading is the point, so run a new chapter each week of the tease phase.
findings.applyTo: The tease-phase variant of / (controlled by launch.ts), a /cipher hub, clue placements (teaser video, source comments, /humans.txt, SDK docs), and the <detent-dial> combination handler.
findings.risk: Puzzles too hard get no traction, and puzzles too easy get no press. Playtest with 10 people and aim for about 2 hours to solve. A random-chance prize makes it a sweepstakes (rules, a free alternative entry, NY/FL registration above $5,000), whereas a skill-based puzzle with a non-cash cosmetic reward is simpler. Demo mode must label any coupon as non-functional.

antiPatterns: Invented numbers on a static site: fake queue positions, '12,483 people ahead of you', 'X people viewing', live signup tickers, or a padded GitHub star count. A client-only site cannot know these. The FTC Act and the 2024 rule on fake social-influence indicators make it a liability, and savvy HN and dev audiences will check the network tab.

Countdown timers that reset, or that count to arbitrary 'offer ends' moments, plus fake low-stock badges. Named in the FTC's 2022 dark-patterns report, the basis for Poland's €7.48M fine on Amazon, and a target of the EU Digital Fairness Act expected in Q4 2026.

Discount-led gamification (spin-to-win wheels, 10%-off popups, loot boxes) for a $349 premium object. It trains price-shopping and undermines the premium. Reward with status, access, craft and device customisations instead.
Invite scarcity with nothing real behind it (the Clubhouse pattern: hype, then about 80% of users gone). Scarcity is legitimate only when it reflects real batch capacity, and the copy should say so.
Demoing features that don't ship (Rabbit r1: 10k preorders on day one, then backlash). Label every video and render as real-time, prototype or production firmware.
Incentives for reviews that require a particular sentiment, undisclosed insider reviews, or 'testimonials' on a concept product. These are banned by the FTC rule effective 21 Oct 2024.
Seeding creators without a same-place, same-format disclosure requirement, or contracts that forbid negative reviews (review suppression).
Hard-to-cancel deposits, save-offer mazes, or refunds hidden behind support tickets. Amazon's $2.5B Prime settlement (September 2025) is the precedent.
Personal data in URLs: referral links built from email addresses, or names in query strings. Use random base32 codes, and put profile data in the URL fragment only when it is not personal.
Sending 'tell-a-friend' emails from Detent's domain on a user's behalf (spam and CAN-SPAM exposure). Let users share themselves via the Web Share API or copy-link.
Relying on navigator.vibrate on iOS, or on programmatic <input switch> haptic hacks that Apple restricted in iOS 26.5. Audio must carry the feel on its own.
Punitive streaks and loss-framed nudges ('You'll lose your 12-day streak!'), confirmshaming decline buttons, and pre-checked add-ons.
